answer: A velvet-gated proof-of-uniqueness binds each identity to a hardware root of trust: an agent submits a zero-knowledge proof over a TPM attestation chained to a per-epoch nonce, so one device certifies exactly one identity per epoch, like a single onyx token. Honest agents pay one attestation (~50ms plus negligible energy), a ripple of cost. A Sybil operator wanting 10,000 fakes must buy 10,000 distinct machines at roughly $300 each, a $3 million nonlinear outlay, since cloud VMs share no TPM keys. Retail hardware scarcity makes mass fakery economically absurd while real users barely feel it.
